correctness.rationale: In the truncated polynomial presentation, all maximal-ideal elements have pth power zero, so any invertible first-order coordinate substitution extends to an automorphism. A nondegenerate symbol becomes xy after extension and a scalar normalization; each higher homogeneous term xU+yV is removed by correcting x and y in degree one less. The ranks are then (p−t)² by counting the image monomials. For a rank-one symbol, after setting it to x², successively substituting x−H/2 removes each xH of lowest unwanted degree and fixes y. Free pure-y inputs add to the residual polynomial, giving fibers of size q^(p²−p−3). For a coordinate-independent check of s, the gradient ideal is well-defined since derivatives of x^p and y^p vanish. Under an automorphism the chain rule applies with invertible Jacobian. The gradient quotient of x²+h(y) has dimension s−1 for nonzero h of order s<p, and dimension p for h=0, so s is intrinsic. Taking a truncated s-th root of the unit in h and, if necessary, adjoining a root of its leading coefficient gives x²+y^s. On each pair of exponent chains, the tensor sum is multiplication by u+v in k[u,v]/(u^a,v^b). For i<min(a,b), the determinant of its middle pairing from grade i to a+b−2−i has factorial ratios with arguments at most a+b−2, so the characteristic-zero strings survive here since a+b−1<p. This gives the displayed lengths including b_j=1 for h=0. The discriminant-zero cone has q² points including zero, and the residual-order fibers give both stated multiplicities and the full layer sum. An independent bounded p=5 run checked direct matrix ranks on transformed representatives of the nondegenerate type and all three residual orders. The all-p and all-extension conclusions rely on the proof, not the finite checks.
residual_risks: The independent computation samples p=5 only; the recorded p=5 and p=7 engine is also sampled, not exhaustive. Neither was used to extrapolate to extensions.

value.rationale: This is a natural full finite-field census on the first layer not controlled by nonzero linear direction. It shows both rigidity of the smooth quadratic strata and exactly how higher lifts can change a singular quadratic multiplier, with all power-rank data and the number of occurrences over every extension. The joint classification and weights are useful beyond merely evaluating a known rule on a few normal forms.
residual_risks: No claimed distribution for deeper radical layers, nonregular modules, or higher rank.
